summary.headline: Liotech H1 FY27 EBITDA margin of 18.46% on INR33.64 crore revenue; management says capacity is near full and capex benefits come in FY28.
summary.overview: H1 FY27 total revenue was INR33.64 crore, with EBITDA of INR6.21 crore (18.46% margin), PBT of INR4.72 crore (14.04%) and PAT of INR3.54 crore (10.51%). Management attributed the margin to lower interest cost after IPO proceeds repaid term loans, and said it targets a 14-15% EBITDA margin going forward. Management said revenue fell about 6% versus last year due to expansion work and manufacturing disruption, while the Shapar plant runs at roughly 88% utilisation on a 12-hour shift. Expansion (two added floors, new CNC laser, bending, pipe-cutting, injection moulding and packaging machinery) is due to be commissioned in the next two to three months, with benefits expected in FY28.

financial_highlights.change: Management said revenue was down about 6% vs last year; no prior-period figure stated
Analyst noted prior half at about 12-13%; management cited ~14-15% historically and ~9% in H2 FY26 PAT context

financial_highlights.value: Aggregate INR36.02 crore: fresh issue INR28.89 crore, OFS INR7.13 crore; net fresh proceeds INR24.28 crore, of which INR24.25 crore utilised as of 30 Sep 2026
financial_highlights.change: Unutilised INR3.24 lakh in escrow and current accounts
Analyst compared with about INR1.2-1.26 crore in H2 FY26; management said this reflects six months vs full year and no headcount cut

segments.name: Architectural and builder's hardware (manufacturing)
segments.commentary: Products include hinges, door kits, tower bolts, aldropes, gate hooks, door stoppers, locks and handles across nine categories with over 150 specifications. Management said about 97% of revenue is in-house manufacturing, with bought-out springs in some assemblies.

guidance_outlook: Targeted EBITDA margin of 14-15% (presentation said 15-16%); management said excess margin may be spent on branding and marketing.
H2 revenue expected to rise as expansion capacity comes on stream in the last quarter; management did not commit to full utilisation of new capacity until Q1 of next year.
Capacity expected to more than double (over 5,000 tonnes per annum vs 2,458 tonnes per annum on an 8-hour basis), with benefits expected in FY28.
Export plans for South Africa, Gulf and European countries, with no timelines or figures given.
capex_capacity: Shapar facility runs at about 88% utilisation, on a 12-hour shift; installed capacity cited as 8 metric tonnes per day on that basis, about 16 tonnes per day on 24 hours.
Expansion adds two floors to take built-up area to about 12,632 sq ft (nearly double); construction expected to finish in 1-2 months, with capex used in the next 2-3 months.
Pending machinery purchase (CNC fibre laser cutting, bending, pipe cutting, injection moulding, automated packaging) is about INR10 crore, held as an FD; expected to complete in about two months.
Labour quarters to rise from 8 to about 20 after modernisation.
Capacity history: 4 tonnes per day in 2023, then roughly doubled through successive capex phases.
demand_pricing: Management said demand exceeds capacity; one domestic purchase order worth about INR6.46 crore (30-day execution) was secured in June 2026, and an advance order book above INR6 crore was cited later in the call.
Present in 9 of 36 states and UTs; plans to add dealers, distributors and states after expansion.
Steel prices stayed firm in H1 FY27; pricing policy passes through steel increases above about 5% and absorbs smaller moves.
Management said selling price rose from about INR100 to INR105 per product, with the increase attributed to inquiry growth after listing.
Receivable days were about 43-44 last year; debtors rose recently with some payment delays; management targets 45 days and MSME norms.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current capacity utilisation and capex timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said utilisation is about 88% and more than 80%, with construction done in 1-2 months and capex used in the last quarter. Capacity will more than double after expansion.

qa_highlights.question: What is the INR60 lakh licence investment on the balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was bought to meet defence tender requirements, refundable in full if the company did not qualify. No defence revenue has been assigned yet.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable are the 18.46% EBITDA margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited lower interest after term-loan repayment from IPO proceeds and said it expects 14-15% EBITDA and 10-11% net margin going forward.

qa_highlights.question: Does entering new states or exports hurt margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pricing is set by its margin structure and there is no negative impact, but gave no figures.

qa_highlights.question: How is raw material risk managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said fluctuations above about 5% are passed to customers, while smaller moves are absorbed by the company.

risks_watch: Revenue fell about 6% in the period due to expansion and manufacturing disruption; H2 recovery depends on the capex timeline and the machinery purchase.
Receivables rose; management said collections are normalising, but the 45-day target is unconfirmed. Watch receivable days in Q3.
Margin sustainability: the H1 EBITDA of 18.46% is well above the 14-15% guided range; management said part of the benefit goes to marketing.
Pending INR10 crore machinery purchase and capacity additions; slippage would delay FY28 volume growth.
Unclear product and export plans: no figures for export revenue, timelines or defence orders.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on demand and capacity but vague on specifics; several answers were incomplete or inconsistent (for example, the 14-15% versus 15-16% margin range and the capacity figures). Answers on working capital, receivables and new-state margins were general, with no numbers.
key_quotes: Our existing Shapar facility operates close to full capacity.
As I mentioned in the presentation, I mentioned 14% to 15% EBITDA margin, which will definitely increase after capex, but we will utilize that funding in marketing and all this stuff.

growth.why: Management guides margins (14-15% EBITDA, 10-11% net) and H2 revenue uplift as ~INR10 crore expansion (more than doubling capacity) comes on stream in roughly 2-3 months, with benefits in FY28; backing is partly specific (capex, one INR6.46 crore order, >INR6 crore order book) but no explicit revenue growth number is given and revenue fell ~6% YoY in H1.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides EBITDA to 14-15% from H1's 18.46%, with the excess to be spent on branding and marketing; the lower interest cost from IPO term-loan repayment is a one-off support, and steel pass-through only applies above about 5% moves.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Expansion (two added floors to ~12,632 sq ft, plus ~INR10 crore CNC laser, bending, pipe-cutting, injection moulding and packaging machinery) is under construction and expected to commission in 2-3 months; capacity to more than double to over 5,000 tpa from 2,458 tpa (8-hour basis).

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Demand exceeds capacity with 88% utilisation and a INR6.46 crore order plus an order book above INR6 crore; capacity more than doubles as expansion comes on stream, though H1 revenue fell about 6% YoY and full use of new capacity is not committed until Q1 next year.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is about 88% on a 12-hour shift and demand exceeds capacity, yet the expansion only lifts capacity from the current base in FY28, so management is likely to keep adding capacity (dealers and states expansion also planned).

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guides 14-15% EBITDA and 10-11% net margin, below the 18.46% H1 EBITDA margin, and said excess margin may go to branding and marketing; no revenue guidance number was given.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 FY27 revenue fell about 6% YoY on expansion work and manufacturing disruption, and management did not commit to full utilisation of the new capacity until Q1 of next year, so H2 volume recovery is not assured; receivables are also rising with payment delays.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product launch was discussed; the new machinery adds capability (injection moulding, packaging) but no product timelines were given, and the defence licence has no revenue assigned yet.

rows.label: Receivable days back to 45 (from 43-44 last year)
rows.why: Debtors rose with some payment delays, and management targets 45 days and MSME norms but gave no confirmed figure.

rows.label: Export and new-state expansion (South Africa, Gulf, Europe; 9 of 36 states today
rows.why: Management plans exports and more dealers and states after expansion, but gave no timelines or revenue figures.

rows.label: Defence tender qualification (INR60 lakh licence)
rows.why: The licence was bought to meet defence tender requirements and is refundable if not qualified, but no defence revenue has been assigned yet.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand exceeding capacity and the expansion timeline, but vague on margin, receivables, export and defence specifics; analysts pressed on the sustainability of the 18.46% EBITDA margin against the 14-15% guide and the inconsistent 14-15% vs 15-16% range.

quality.why: Management said H1 FY27 revenue fell about 6% versus last year due to expansion work and manufacturing disruption, so there is no revenue growth to explain; the only growth-related items are a claimed ~5% selling price increase (INR100 to INR105, unverified) and a margin lift attributed to lower interest after IPO debt repayment, which is a profit-level driver rather than revenue growth.
